national_indicator_definition: The circular material use rate, also known as the circularity rate, measures the share of material recycled and fed back into the economy in overall material use. It is calculated as the ratio of circular use of materials to overall material use. A higher value indicates that a larger share of secondary raw materials is used as a substitute for primary raw materials, thereby reducing the need for the extraction of natural resources.
national_rationale: The indicator is produced in accordance with the quality standards of European statistics. The data source is the European Statistical System (ESS), and the original Eurostat dataset is ENV_AC_CUR. Eurostat disseminates the indicator on the basis of data provided by countries. Circular use of materials is estimated on the basis of the amount of waste recycled in domestic recovery facilities, adjusted for imports and exports of waste intended for recovery. Overall material use is calculated as the sum of domestic material consumption (DMC) and circular use of materials. The indicator is updated annually.
national_methodology_characteristics: The indicator covers overall material use in the economy and makes it possible to monitor the contribution of recycled materials to reducing the consumption of primary raw materials. Data are collected annually and allow comparisons between EU Member States. The time series for the EU aggregate starts in 2004, while data for Member States and individual material categories are available from 2010 onwards.
national_long_objective: In March 2020, the European Commission adopted the new Circular Economy Action Plan (CEAP), which aims to reduce pressure on natural resources and accelerate the transition to a circular economy. The plan covers the entire life cycle of products, from design and production to consumption and waste management, with a particular focus on waste prevention, reuse and material recycling. The 8th Environment Action Programme, adopted in 2022, further emphasises the transition towards a climate-neutral, resource-efficient and regenerative economy. Within the EU Sustainable Development Goals framework, the target is to double the circular material use rate by 2030 compared with 2020.
